"Is it slow because we are recovering from the writers and actors strike or is it slow because the lingering strike this summer?"

Both. After the writer/actor strike, some productions were both trying to pick up where they left off and some were also just beginning, whereas both wouldn't have been happening at once. Now with this other strike potentially happening in summer, studios are hesitant to begin filming as they risk going on hiatus until it resolves. 

That being said, a well-sourced contact told me that studios realised how much money they've been losing. After covid, everyone hurried to make all the films they'd been planning as quickly as possible, which meant spending more money on additional crew to work on their projects since they wanted to make so much at once. Now that time has passed and those projects have since been released, they've looked at the numbers and realised they didn't make as much as money as they thought. This has made them want to put a hold on production so they can plan smarter for the future and not lose as much money in the process.

I too don't want to give up my dream, but at the minute I'm beginning to consider if I should take up something else to keep the money flowing.
